title: No More Slop – swyx
talk_summary: This is a short conference keynote about the cultural problem of 'slop' (low-quality, inauthentic, inaccurate output) in AI-generated content and code, not a technical talk. It offers only a few concrete mechanisms: explicitly prompting models not to produce slop, using sub-agents to fight context rot, and keeping human-designed boundaries with AI filling in between.

takeaways.what_they_do: They cite a prompt/skill set that explicitly acknowledges slop and instructs Claude not to produce it, which measurably improves output quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they actually acknowledge slop and tell cloud not to produce slop and it actually improves significantly from left to right

takeaways.what_they_do: Delegate work to sub-agents so the main agent's context stays clean, rather than accumulating everything in one long context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also use sub agents to fight context rot

takeaways.technique: Modularity: human-designed boundaries, AI fills in
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep clear boundaries on what is human-designed and let the AI code everything in between, per Greg Brockman's modularity advice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep clear boundaries on what is human designed and let the AI code everything in between

takeaways.what_they_do: Criticizes vendors who boast about long autonomous runtimes without reporting whether the code was good, arguing autonomy needs accountability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't want autonomy without accountability
